papers.title: Passenger's ledger
lines: Arrived in Boston in 1847 with the clothes I wore and a fiddle. Landed hungry, left hungrier, and found work by Thursday.
My granddaughter will be a nurse. My great-grandson will be mayor. Neither will know I played.

papers.title: Tea-party flyer
lines: Boston, December 1773. Three ships, three hundred and forty-two chests of tea, and a lot of people who had had enough.
Nobody was hurt, save the tea. The cold-water harbour has never been the same since.

trail.clue: A tea-chest lid is said to lie near the statue, where someone hid a pocketful of coin.

papers.title: Recipe note
lines: Boston baked beans: navy beans, salt pork, molasses, patience. Eight hours in a slow oven.
A Saturday supper, a Sunday breakfast, and a Monday argument with the cat.

papers.title: Walking tour card
lines: Follow the red line on the pavement. It leads from church to churchyard to a ship with a good name.
Do not stop at the first bar. There are at least four better ones further on.
